reproduction_target: Capture-bisulfite-sequencing (capture-BSseq) methylome analysis of the 5' end (TSS / start-codon, 300 bp windows) of ~100k high-confidence wheat genes in developing grain of natural and synthetic allohexaploid wheat: (i) an upstream in-silico capture-probe design pipeline (15 Triticeae assemblies shredded with GenomeTools, mapped with bwa mem, filtered with samtools/blat, consensus contigs assembled in Geneious 6.1 via a custom python MSA-extraction script); (ii) the main methylome pipeline (Trim Galore -> Bismark/Bowtie2 alignment to Chinese Spring v1.0 -> bismark_methylation_extractor -> methylKit filtering and methylation-level summarisation -> genomation ScoreMatrixBin metaprofiles -> methylKit methseg segmentation -> methylKit calculateDiffMeth DMR/DMC calling); (iii) integrative statistics relating TSS/SC methylation to transcription (Pearson/Wilcoxon correlations, triad homeolog-contribution classification, DEG-DMR Venn overlaps with exact hypergeometric and chi-square tests) using transcriptome/DEG data carried over from Banouh et al. (2023). Plant material production (reciprocal synthetic allohexaploid crosses), DNA extraction, SureSelect capture + bisulfite conversion, library preparation and NovaSeq6000 sequencing are wet-lab (W, out of scope for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis decomposition from the bioRxiv JATS XML (fetched by curl into /tmp/stage1_10.1101_2025.10.08.680649/paper.xml after WebFetch returned HTTP 403; title-phrase check 'not globally associated with transcription' matched, so the fetch is the correct paper). 19 C-steps, 4 W-steps. The paper contains NO code availability statement and cites NO code repository (no GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Zenodo/Software Heritage URL appears anywhere in the full text), so there was no repo landing page or README prose to read; per the protocol this absence is recorded as a finding and no web search for a repository was performed. Software version pins are essentially absent: Trim Galore, Bismark, Bowtie2, bismark_methylation_extractor, methylKit, genomation, bwa mem, samtools, blat and GenomeTools are all named without any version. The single exact software pin in the paper is the proprietary Geneious 6.1 (probe-contig assembly), scored Version=1 with the rubric's explicit 'commercial but exactly pinned -> 1 license-gated' rule. Reference resources ARE pinned (Chinese Spring annotation v1.1, Chinese Spring reference genome v1.0 - note the paper itself uses v1.1 for annotation but v1.0 for alignment; Ae. tauschii v4.0; Svevo v2; chloroplast NC_002762.1 / NC_022133.1), but the Version axis here scores software-environment pinning, so resource pinning alone does not lift Version above 0. BOUNDARY CALL on capture_claim: exactly one exact software version pin exists (Geneious 6.1) while zero of the ten main-pipeline tools are pinned and no lockfile/container/conda spec is claimed; 'floating' was chosen over 'exact_pins_partial' because no analysis-pipeline tool is pinned at all. Either classification yields stage2_candidate=false under protocol v0.2.6, so the choice is score-neutral for the gate.

steps.label: TSS/SC target definition from the Chinese Spring v1.1 high-confidence gene annotation (first position of the 5'-UTR treated as TSS for 68,731/107,891 HC genes; start codon used for the remaining 36.3%; 300 bp window, 150 bp up/downstream) - no script or tool named

GenomeTools shredder - shred 15 chromosome-level Triticeae assemblies into 500 bp fragments with a 250 bp sliding step; no GenomeTools version pinned, and the full list of 15 assemblies is not enumerated with accessions
bwa mem - map all shredded assembly fragments onto the Chinese Spring v1.1 reference into a single BAM; no bwa version pinned, no non-default flags stated
samtools - filter out fragment alignments with mapping quality <20; no samtools version pinned

Custom python script - extract per-genome consensus sequences around each TSS/SC from the BAM as multiple sequence alignments (150 bp upstream, 150 bp downstream); script not deposited and not linked anywhere in the paper

Geneious 6.1 (Biomatters) - re-assemble upstream and downstream fragments into probe-candidate contigs allowing no gaps and up to 3% mismatches within >=120 bp overlaps; commercial GUI software with an EXACT version pin (the only exact software pin in the paper)

Probe-candidate filtering - remove (i) upstream/downstream redundant candidates, (ii) candidates mapping to the wheat chloroplast genome with <=10% mismatches, (iii) candidates with valid bwa mem alignments to <8 of the assemblies, (iv) candidates with more off-target than on-target blat hits (blat -fastMap -minScore=80); yields 200,495 consensus probes. No blat/bwa versions, no glue script deposited

Trim Galore - adapter removal and quality filtering of the 18 directional capture-BSseq libraries (reads with length <20 and unpaired reads eliminated); no Trim Galore/cutadapt version, no explicit flags or adapter sequences

Bismark alignment - align trimmed reads to the Chinese Spring reference genome v1.0 in directional mode using the Bowtie2 mapper with 'pre-defined settings'; no Bismark or Bowtie2 version pinned and 'pre-defined settings' is not expanded (note: annotation used for targets is v1.1, alignment reference is stated as v1.0)
bismark_methylation_extractor - extract per-cytosine methylation calls retaining only reads with a unique best alignment score; no version pinned, no explicit flag list

Bisulfite conversion-efficiency estimation - align filtered reads to chloroplast genomes (Chinese Spring NC_002762.1 for Recital/Langdon/Jx109/Jx87/Lx109-C2; Ae. tauschii NC_022133.1 for 109xL-C2/109xL-C4/Tauschii-109/Tauschii-87) and compute conversion rate = converted C / total analysed C x 100; aligner version not pinned

methylKit filterByCoverage + methylation-level summarisation - remove bases above the 99.99th coverage percentile; mean methylation level (Schultz et al. 2012) from positions with >=10x for single-cytosine/global analyses, weighted methylation level from cytosines with coverage >=3 for region-based analyses; no methylKit or R version pinned

Binomial test of CHH methylation significance against the per-sample bisulfite non-conversion rate (10-16% of CHH sites significant); no software/package named, no significance threshold stated in Methods
genomation ScoreMatrixBin - summarise fine-scale methylation around TSS/SC in 10 bp bins; no genomation version pinned

methylKit methseg - change-point segmentation of target regions into variable-length homogeneous-methylation segments, identified from pooled parental data (Tauschii-109, Langdon), each segment required to contain >=3 CpG sites at >=10x coverage; no methylKit version pinned

methylKit calculateDiffMeth - DMR/DMC identification between synthetics and parents (logistic regression with overdispersion correction, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR; methylation difference >25% and FDR <0.01), run over both the 300 bp fixed target windows and the methseg segments, each cytosine context separately; no methylKit version pinned

Methylation vs transcription vs centromere-distance statistics - Pearson correlations and Wilcoxon tests across samples, subgenomes and cytosine contexts (methylation-distance, methylation-expression, expression-distance; 2 Mb windows with 1 Mb step for chromosome scans); no statistical software or package named, expression (TPM) data taken from Banouh et al. (2023) without an accession in this paper

Triad / homeolog-expression-contribution classification (balanced 16.7-66.7% of triad total, otherwise suppressed or dominant) 'as described in Banouh et al. (2023)', compared against weighted mean TSS/SC methylation per gene; triad definition and expression quantification are externalised to the prior paper, no code or version

DEG-DMR / DEG-DMC association testing - Venn-diagram overlaps between DEGs (from Banouh et al. 2023, restricted to genes with >=10x BSseq coverage) and DMRs from both DMR methods, tested with the exact hypergeometric test with normal approximation and the chi-square test; no software or package named for the Venn/statistics

Plant material - production of five synthetic allohexaploids from reciprocal crosses and successive generations (109xL-C2, 109xL-C4, Lx109-C2, Jx87-S5, Jx109-S5), parental genotypes and natural hexaploid Recital; growth conditions delegated to Banouh et al. (2023)

Genomic DNA extraction from developing grain (liquid-nitrogen grinding, NaCl/Tris/EDTA/SDS buffer, phenol:chloroform:isoamylalcohol 25:24:1, sodium-acetate/ethanol precipitation, RNase A treatment, Qiagen silica spin columns), two biological replicates per sample
Sequence capture with Agilent SureSelect Custom Tier6 probes followed by bisulfite conversion with the EZ DNA Methylation-Gold Kit (ZYMO Research)

Library preparation with the SureSelectXT Methyl Reagent kit (Agilent) with post-conversion multiplexing (PGTB, France) and sequencing of 18 directional libraries on NovaSeq6000 (2x150) at Genotoul, France, to a theoretical target depth of 40x

headline.static_readiness: 0/19 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 1/19 computational steps (C6, Geneious 6.1 probe-contig assembly - the only exactly version-pinned software in the paper, scored Version=1 license-gated per the rubric's commercial-but-exactly-pinned rule). The remaining 18/19 C-steps cap at NI because no version is pinned for any of Trim Galore, Bismark, Bowtie2, bismark_methylation_extractor, methylKit, genomation, bwa mem, samtools, blat or GenomeTools, and because the statistical steps (C13, C17, C19) name no package at all. C5 additionally has Code=0 (custom python script for MSA extraction, not deposited). No environment lockfile, container digest or conda specification is claimed anywhere, and the paper carries NO code availability statement and NO code repository URL, so even a Stage-2 pass could not lift any step to R-star on environment grounds: there is no environment to verify and no code to verify it against. The BSseq raw data themselves are properly deposited (SRA BioProject PRJNA1247774, resolvable), so the ceiling here is set entirely by the code and version axes, not by data.
headline.coverage: 19 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS full-text Methods prose (probe design 7 steps: C1-C7; methylome pipeline 9 steps: C8-C16; integrative statistics 3 steps: C17-C19). 4 wet-lab steps (synthetic allohexaploid production, DNA extraction, SureSelect capture + bisulfite conversion, library prep + NovaSeq6000 sequencing) counted in W and marked OOS. Transcriptome/DEG inputs to C17-C19 originate from Banouh et al. (2023) and carry no accession in this paper.

gaps.where: Whole paper - there is no Code Availability statement
gaps.missing: No analysis code is deposited or linked anywhere. A full-text scan for github / gitlab / bitbucket / zenodo / figshare / software heritage returned zero hits; the only code-related phrase in the paper is 'a custom python script' in the probe-design section. The DATA AVAILABILITY STATEMENT covers sequencing reads only. Consequently no repository landing page or README prose existed to read at Stage 1, and no environment-capture claim of any kind could be evaluated.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the probe-design scripts and the methylome/statistics analysis scripts in a public repository archived to Zenodo or Software Heritage with a resolvable DOI, and add a Code Availability statement pointing to it.

gaps.where: Every computational step except C6 (probe design C1-C5, C7; methylome pipeline C8-C16; statistics C17-C19)
gaps.missing: 2a - no software version is recorded for any pipeline tool: Trim Galore, Bismark, Bowtie2, bismark_methylation_extractor, methylKit, genomation (ScoreMatrixBin), bwa mem, samtools, blat and GenomeTools are all named without a version, and R itself is never versioned. The statistical steps (binomial test, Pearson/Wilcoxon correlations, Venn diagrams, exact hypergeometric and chi-square tests) name no package at all. No lockfile (renv.lock, conda-lock, pixi.lock), no container image or digest, and no conda environment specification is claimed. Reference resources are pinned (Chinese Spring annotation v1.1, alignment reference v1.0, Ae. tauschii v4.0, Svevo v2, chloroplast NC_002762.1 / NC_022133.1) but resource pinning does not substitute for software pinning.
gaps.how_to_close: Report exact versions for every tool and R package in Methods or a versions table, and ship a renv.lock / conda-lock / container digest that closes the whole R + command-line stack.

gaps.where: C5 - probe design, consensus MSA extraction
gaps.missing: The 'custom python script' that extracts per-genome consensus sequences (150 bp upstream / 150 bp downstream of each TSS/SC) from the merged BAM is neither deposited nor described in enough detail to be re-implemented deterministically; the 200,495-probe design that defines the entire target space of the study depends on it.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the script, and publish the final probe/target coordinate set (BED or FASTA) so downstream analyses can be reproduced even without re-running probe design.

gaps.where: C17, C18, C19 - all transcription-related analyses
gaps.missing: The transcriptome data, TPM quantification, triad definition, homeolog-contribution computation and DEG calls are all externalised to Banouh et al. (2023). This paper gives no accession for the RNA-seq data and no description of the expression pipeline; the triad classification is cited as 'used as described in' the prior paper. The methylation-vs-transcription conclusions - the paper's central claim - therefore cannot be reproduced from this paper alone.
gaps.how_to_close: Restate the RNA-seq accession, the expression-quantification pipeline and the triad-definition procedure in this paper's Methods, and deposit the derived TPM / DEG / triad tables as supplementary data.

gaps.missing: Geneious 6.1 (Biomatters) is proprietary, licence-gated and a legacy release; the assembly step (no gaps, <=3% mismatch, >=120 bp overlap) can only be reproduced by a party holding a licence for that specific version. Per the rubric this is Version=1 license-gated, not a Version=0 unknown-tool failure, but it does impose a proprietary ceiling on exact reproduction of the probe design.
gaps.how_to_close: Re-implement the contig assembly with an open-source assembler, or publish the resulting probe contigs so the proprietary step need not be re-executed.

gaps.where: C8-C16 - sample-to-run correspondence for the deposited BSseq data
gaps.missing: The 18 libraries (9 genotypes x 2 biological replicates) are deposited under BioProject PRJNA1247774, but the mapping from library/run accession to genotype, replicate and chloroplast reference used for the conversion-rate estimate is carried in Supplementary Tables S1/S3/S4 rather than in the main text, so re-running the pipeline requires the supplement.
gaps.how_to_close: Include a machine-readable sample sheet (run accession -> genotype -> replicate -> reference used) alongside the deposited reads.

gaps.missing: The Methods use the Chinese Spring v1.1 annotation to define TSS/SC targets and the probe design maps against the 'Chinese Spring v1.1 reference', but the BSseq reads are stated to be aligned to 'the Chinese spring reference genome v1.0'. No accession or download URL is given for either assembly build, so the exact reference FASTA cannot be resolved unambiguously.
gaps.how_to_close: Give the exact IWGSC assembly/annotation release identifiers and download URLs for the assembly used in each step, and reconcile the v1.0 / v1.1 discrepancy.

gaps.missing: Synthetic allohexaploid production (reciprocal crosses, successive generations), grain DNA extraction, Agilent SureSelect Custom Tier6 capture with EZ DNA Methylation-Gold bisulfite conversion, SureSelectXT Methyl library preparation and NovaSeq6000 2x150 sequencing are physical sequence-generation steps, out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W (4) and marked OOS, not verdicted.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; the deposited raw reads (SRA PRJNA1247774) are the reproducible entry point into the computational pipeline.
